items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: a guy named Frankie Dunlop was the drummer, formerly with Thelonious Monk, an incredible drummer.

ctx.x: We’ll have to put an “X” on this one. Okay. Let me repeat that. That feeling of the power of music, that a number of times I’ve seen you in front of a group of kids now, I can tell that that’s pretty important to you to try to get across to them.

Yeah, well you know I think ultimately, Monk, it’s no good to have something and you can’t share it. And from the beginning, whenever I’ve learned something that has affected my life I’ve immediately wanted to share it with someone. And since I come from a family of teachers, I also feel that I’m a teacher sort of. I think really ultimately we all are teachers, but when I find a piece of music that affects me, when I learn something new, I immediately want to share it with somebody. But you know what?
